title: Putting good energy into action
summary: Xcel Energy’s Day of Service unites communities to make an impact
body_markdown:
Each September, Xcel Energy’s Day of Service brings together thousands of employees, retirees and community members to participate in meaningful volunteer events across our service territory. Originally created to honor the people and communities impacted by 9/11, this recognition has grown into a lasting celebration of service — and a reminder of the difference communities can make when they stand together.


This year marked our 16th annual Day of Service, uniting more than 2,400 volunteers to support 100 nonprofit organizations across our eight states. Together, participants dedicated over 7,400 hours of service across 109 projects, resulting in an economic impact of $268,000.

More highlights from this year’s event include:


Minnesota, North Dakota and South Dakota: Over 1,030 volunteers dedicated 3,174 hours, serving 47 nonprofit projects and generating $114,708 in economic impact.


Wisconsin and Michigan: 191 volunteers contributed 825 hours, serving 10 projects with an economic impact of $29,816.


Colorado: 815 volunteers dedicated 2,750 volunteer hours, serving 44 events with an economic impact of $99,385.


Texas and New Mexico: 131 volunteers contributed 675 hours, serving 8 projects with an economic impact of $24,395.


This deep-rooted tradition is a powerful moment to give back to the communities we serve, but the spirit of service is carried forward by our teams every day. Throughout the year, employees dedicate their time, talents and passion to hundreds of volunteering and giving opportunities across the communities where they live and work. Learn more about Xcel Energy’s[commitment to volunteerism.](https://corporate.my.xcelenergy.com/s/community/engagement/day-of-service)
